svg.title: How breadth-first search spreads
svg.desc: An animation of breadth-first search on a grid of 8 by 6 intersections, bigger than the floor grid so the shape shows, with (0, 0) at the bottom-left. A wall of four blocked intersections stands at x = 3 from y = 1 to y = 4, leaving gaps at the top and bottom. The search starts at S, (0, 4), and the destination D is (7, 4), on the other side of the wall. Each intersection lights up with its step count from S the moment the search first reaches it: 1 for the neighbors of S, then 2, then 3, so the numbers spread out from S in even rings, like a ripple. The ripple flows through the gap at the top of the wall and bends around it, and also around the bottom. When D is taken off the list the search stops, and the walk-back from D to S is drawn in red: up, along the top through the gap, and back down to D, 9 steps.
